content.title: About
content.content: Rice flour is a finely milled white rice product without added vitamins or minerals. It has a neutral flavor, light texture, and is commonly used in gluten‑free cooking, baking, and as a thickening agent.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice flour is made from polished white rice, with the bran and germ removed.
It is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
In Asian cuisine it is used for noodles, dumpling wrappers, and traditional desserts.
Rice flour has a higher glycemic index than wheat flour, so it should be consumed in moderation.
It is also used in cosmetics as an absorbent and gentle exfoliant.

items.title: Rich source of carbohydrates
items.content: Rice flour provides easily digestible carbs that quickly supply energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: It contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Although not a complete protein, it contributes to daily protein intake.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Ideal for those who must avoid gluten.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The lack of bran makes it gentle on the stomach, useful for sensitive digestion.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Lacks certain micronutrients
items.content: Unenriched rice flour is low in iron, B‑vitamins, and fiber.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience allergic reactions.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Rice can accumulate trace arsenic; choose reputable brands and avoid excessive use.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rice flour is used in gluten‑free baking (bread, cakes, cookies), as a coating, for thickening sauces and soups, and in Asian dishes such as noodles and dumplings. It can be blended with other gluten‑free flours to improve texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rice flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat oxidation.
